acceptance: tsbs_devops/schema.py, joinorder/schema.py and the CoffeeShop seeds trigger the gate.
A test fails when a generator gains an ungated first-party import.
context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
The gate table on #4322 misses inputs that change SF 1 bytes: `benchbox/core/tsbs_devops/schema.py` (TABLE_ORDER and schema imported by the generator), `benchbox/core/joinorder/schema.py` (imported by joinorder_synthetic's generator) and the CoffeeShop seed files under `benchbox/data/coffeeshop/`. `docs/internal/generator-volume-gate.md` does not list them as limits.

## Change
For each of the nine gated benchmarks, list the generator's transitive first-party imports and data files and decide gate or documented limit; add the three known inputs to the table and the CI filter.

## Decision gates
If the import closure is large for a benchmark, stop and propose a rule (for example a test that derives the table from imports) to the owner instead of hand-listing.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the table, the filter and the doc agree; a test asserts each generator module's first-party imports are either gated or named in an explicit allowlist with a reason.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed.
- The implementer never resolves review threads on its own pull request; the reviewer or the owner does.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, and no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
